questions.text: In 'Rinse and dry your hands', which specific hand-drying methods should be listed instead of a cloth towel?
questions.why: Cloth towels are prohibited in food service environments to prevent cross-contamination.

questions.text: How should 'Use hand sanitizer if soap is unavailable' be modified to comply with the requirement that soap must always be used?
questions.why: Hand sanitizer is not a legal substitute for soap and water for required employee handwashing.

questions.text: What type of sink must be used for this procedure to meet health and safety regulations?
questions.why: Employees must use dedicated handwashing sinks rather than those used for food prep or dishwashing.

questions.text: Besides the hands and wrists, which parts of the arms must also be scrubbed?
questions.why: Food safety codes require scrubbing all exposed portions of the arms.

questions.text: What is the correct way to turn off faucets or use dispensers to avoid recontaminating hands after washing?
questions.why: Avoiding contact with manual handles after washing is essential for proper hygiene.

questions.text: What is the required temperature for the running water in 'Wet your hands and apply soap'?
questions.why: The water must be at a specific temperature to comply with safety standards.

questions.text: How much soap should be applied during the first step?
questions.why: The amount of soap used affects the thoroughness of the cleaning.

questions.text: In 'Rinse and dry your hands', how many seconds should the rinse phase last?
questions.why: Sufficient rinsing time is required to remove all soap and contaminants.
